# Houston

> Houston is a free, cross-platform desktop coding agent that you point at your own AI model. Give it a project folder and it reads, edits, searches, and runs code, with every consequential action gated by an approval flow and, where the OS supports it, shell commands run in a sandbox. It runs locally and collects no analytics or telemetry from the app.

## What it is

- Status: beta. Houston is pre-1.0, so expect rough edges, and settings or behavior may change between releases.
- Type: desktop application (macOS, Windows, Linux), built with Electron, React, and TypeScript.
- Price: free. You bring your own model API keys, or run a local model; you pay only your provider's usage, never Houston.
- License: open source under the Apache License 2.0. Use, modify, and redistribute it, commercially or not, keeping the license and copyright notices and the NOTICE file. The Houston name and logo are not licensed.
- Bring your own model: Claude (Anthropic, or via Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, or Microsoft Foundry), GPT (OpenAI), Gemini (Google), any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and local models via Ollama or LM Studio. Switch models per conversation.
- Privacy: runs on your device; no in-app telemetry. Data leaves only to providers you configure, when you use a feature that reaches the network. Our download host keeps aggregate download and update-check counts for released files (no personal data, no in-app tracking).
- Safety: choose an approval mode from review-every-action to full autonomy; shell commands are sandboxed where the OS supports it.
- Isolation: shell commands run under Seatbelt (macOS) or bubblewrap (Linux, when installed), with writes confined to the project and network limited to an allowlist once granted. Each chat in a git repo runs in its own worktree, and any turn's file changes can be reverted in one click.
- Team controls: repos can ship tighten-only permission rules, elevating project config is ignored until the folder is trusted, and admins can lock a machine-wide policy.
- Supply chain: macOS builds are signed and notarized; every release ships cosign-signed checksums, an SBOM, and SLSA build provenance.

## Key capabilities

- Agentic tools: read, write, edit, patch, search files, run shell, inspect git, fetch and search the web, and drive pull requests. Pure reads run concurrently; writes and commands stay sequential.
- Structural code search with a bundled ripgrep and ast-grep (syntax-tree matching), plus type-aware navigation (definitions, references, rename) and post-edit error checks through any installed language server (TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, C/C++).
- See its own localhost: start a dev server, screenshot the page, read the console, and iterate. A live preview panel docks beside the chat.
- Subagents (read-only research, or approval-gated edits) and adversarial multi-agent review of your diff for correctness, security, and quality.
- Clients: the desktop app, an interactive terminal, one-shot headless runs for scripts and CI, an Agent Client Protocol server (`houston --acp`) for ACP-capable editors, and a GitHub Action that answers @houston mentions, reviews pull requests, and fixes failed CI on your own runners.
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers over stdio, HTTP, or SSE, including OAuth sign-in for hosted servers; custom agents (read-only by default) and on-demand skills defined in Markdown.

## Platforms

- macOS 13 Ventura or newer (Apple Silicon and Intel)
- Windows 10 or newer (x64)
- Linux x64 (glibc 2.35+, e.g. Ubuntu 22.04+)
- Standalone terminal CLI for macOS, Windows and Linux (x64 or Arm) with Node 22+:
  - Homebrew: `brew install houston-code/tap/houston`
  - npm: `npm install -g @houston-code/cli`
  - Install script: `curl -fsSL https://houstoncode.ai/install.sh | sh`
